rites.name: Seroriles
rites.text: Seroriles is a sealed sovereign-rune of the Ki realm, carved by a lost smith-god to hold the stellar tides in their courses. Its inscriptions were never meant to be read by mortal eyes, and each stroke still pulls at the dark between suns.

rites.name: Tiralaeno
rites.text: Tiralaeno is the concept of a rooted, growing resonance that first gave the Singing its shape, when the world's roots were still condensing into soil and sap. It is understood as the pull that draws small seeds toward light and binds groves into kingdoms.

rites.name: Feneste
rites.text: Feneste is the concept of a sounding that gathers the first roots of Tianausanum into form, a hum that tells loose matter where to settle. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall split the old bonds between peoples and place, Feneste was the thread that stitched the broken ground back together.

rites.name: Lisernus
rites.text: A personal skill that lets a person convey intentions to creatures that have no spoken language. It cannot carry subtle or intricate meanings, since the creatures' minds remain unchanged.

rites.name: Amistialia
rites.text: Amistialia is a concept-born sovereign of the Ki realm in the third age of Tianausanum, a sovereign whose purpose was set long before she woke. She was made to coax a sleeping order of guardians toward their long-deferred labor, and she carries that unfinished work across the ages.

rites.name: Crorene
rites.text: Crorene is the concept of a threshold, the moment a petition is granted or refused in the Courts of Tianausanum. Within the Age of the first sovereign it is said to hold the weight of every door raised between worlds, and its name is spoken before any council convenes.

rites.name: Joruldon
rites.text: Joruldon is the concept of a binding oath sworn before the Courts, the principle that a vow made in front of witnesses can hold a door shut across worlds. In the Age of Sundering it was the thread the council wove to keep landfall from tearing old bonds apart.

rites.name: Neniallia
rites.text: A discipline in which a practitioner joins a venture that offers no hope of escape, accepting that death is the expected outcome. Those who master it treat the willingness to fall as their greatest technique.

rites.name: Tauses
rites.text: A divine favor that marks someone as blessed by the sky-dwelling powers. It brings a variety of different effects to the one who carries it.

rites.name: Nasaunium
rites.text: A master's unique footwork creates duplicate forms that strike in rapid succession, too fast for onlookers to see. The practitioner casts no shadow while performing it.

rites.name: Vauniallor
rites.text: A disciplined craft that shapes the flow of raw substance, letting practitioners redirect and rework the material makeup of things. It is counted among the recognized schools of arcane working.

rites.name: Valeornorus
rites.text: A binding force that presses down on foes with crushing weight, holding them fast so they cannot step or stir.

rites.name: Rarellia
rites.text: A ritual technique that lets its user draw weapons and treasures out of the earth using clay, copying the finest crafts of the world. It can be used across great distances and even makes golden walls that resist the strikes it creates.

rites.name: Maullia
rites.text: A discipline of combat mastery practiced while mounted on a steed. It is taught across many schools of riders who fight from the saddle.

rites.name: Seriasum
rites.text: A bodiless discipline that channels desire through unseen force. Practitioners cultivate a quality of formlessness tied to an ancient figure who is known for being without a body.

rites.name: Rilianum
rites.text: A rare inherited rite that wakes once a bearer has fallen. Whoever slays the sovereign beast or her echoes has every lingering curse lifted from them, mirroring the beast's strange habit of cherishing those who end her, a quirk that brings her own disadvantage yet quietly entertains her.

rites.name: Lilontor
rites.text: A sacred spear-dance that forcefully cleanses the summer demon of deceit and fleeting passion. Its spinning motion pulls the user's body into a tornado of cursed wind, at the cost of self-destruction.

rites.name: Tosintus
rites.text: A battlefield faculty that grants its bearer an instinctive grasp of tactics. It reflects the sharp wartime intuition of a legendary commander renowned as the finest of his age.

rites.name: Meoriasum
rites.text: A bearer of unbending conviction first judges whether a foe is wicked or virtuous, then briefly reshapes that foe into a winged serpent of great might. The sacred cloth and cloak serve only as a focus, and the power wakes solely through the bearer's steadfast belief.

rites.name: Serianastor
rites.text: A skill that marks a being as beloved by a divine woman. It shows that a goddess holds a special favor toward that one.

rites.name: Vostia
rites.text: A cursed strike delivered by a sword soaked in ancient vengeance. It erases everything it touches, reducing the target and its existence to nothing, and it reshapes into one enormous blade when unleashed.

rites.name: Santium
rites.text: A divine favor that marks one mortal as beloved by a masculine deity. Its binding strength matches that of its feminine counterpart, bringing a comparable weight of burden.

rites.name: Lintanum
rites.text: A dark state that lets its bearer shrug off countless lethal blows and keep fighting unhindered. The bearer can no longer tell whether they remain living or have passed beyond.

rites.name: Nerontus
rites.text: A rare gift that cancels almost every kind of enchanted working, including unusual and unconventional ones. Practitioners leave spells unable to take hold around them.

rites.name: Ameorum
rites.text: A broad skill that lets its holder show ability across many different crafts, from fighting techniques to fine arts and matters of the heart.

rites.name: Serisaullia
rites.text: A binding craft that presses hard against the inner channels of another's arcane flow. It can force that flow to stall or bend under the practitioner's will.

rites.name: Sastintor
rites.text: A withering power that unmakes whatever mortal hands have built and the rules that favor their kind. It was first wielded by a clan of primal hunters who called it the beast's sovereignty.

rites.name: Feneston
rites.text: Feneston is the concept of the wall that holds a people together, understood in Tianausanum as a living bond rather than mere stone. In the Walled Age it was carried through orders, churches and the first crossings of rivers, shaping how groves and young kingdoms kept their borders.

rites.name: Viria
rites.text: A bearer draws a single gathered approval into a sudden surge of might, swelling in stature for a brief span and crushing foes with overwhelming force.

rites.name: Montallanum
rites.text: Montallanum is a hidden covenant of the three ancient lineages, a lattice of sigils that can compel a bound spirit to end its own existence, unlocking the final conduit to the primal source. The sigils are etched upon the heart of the chosen champion and only the true victor of the sacred chalice may activate them, forcing the spirit's self‑annihilation and completing the seven‑spirit convergence ritual.

rites.name: Mesorium
rites.text: Mesorium is a crystalline lattice-engine that hums with the memory of forged blades, drawing ambient heat into resonant chords that can lift a vessel out of its orbit. Its hidden keel is said to sing when a rival empire's weapons are near, and the Ki tribunals have forbidden its full activation for three ages.

rites.name: Oralor
rites.text: Oralor is a Ki-realm warden-spirit that shepherds dying sparks toward the cold rim of the valley of Tenmoro. Its brief appearances leave hushed villages behind, and only a few lamplighters know how to bargain with it.

rites.name: Nauntesum
rites.text: Nauntesum is a spear-bearing concept of the Ki realm in the second age of Tianausanum, forged to be wielded by warriors touched by the sky's favor. Its barbed head is said to pierce any defense once struck, though every victory it grants has been paid for with the blood of kin.

rites.name: Lauror
rites.text: Lauror is a concept held in the Ki realm of Tianausanum, the shared riding art of wandering sovereigns and their companions during the third age of the E6 era. Its bearers ride swift moth-like steeds through the land, nudging the hearts and minds of those they pass, and the art is passed hand to hand across generations.

rites.name: Orinia
rites.text: Orinia is a drifting engine-court of the Ki realm, a vaulted hall of nine mirrored cathedrals that hangs above a silent star and feeds on the attention of those who gaze into it. Its keepers can seal a visitor inside a looping recital until the audience forgets how to leave, and every hour spent captive dulls the captive's will and armour alike.

rites.name: Coraunum
rites.text: Coraunum is a concept-realm entry named for a faded oath-engine that hums beneath the Ki-tides of Tianausanum. Its mind burns hot enough to lose its sense of self whenever a wound is opened in the realm's shared memory. Scholars who study it describe a nature closer to a storm that remembers grief than to any settled person.

rites.name: Vianus
rites.text: Vianus is a concept in the Ki realm of Tianausanum, a ward-like principle that turns incoming arcane force aside rather than fighting it head-on. Its bearers are said to bend curses back into the sky so completely that even the oldest workings find no purchase. Scholars of the E6 era still debate whether Vianus is a power, a discipline, or a wound left by the first sorcerers.

rites.name: Coreolor
rites.text: Coreolor is a sealed conceptual discipline in the Ki realm of Tianausanum, a ruling art that answers only to the pure hush beyond ordinary reason. Its practitioners are said to pierce into the still center of the world's hidden foundation, and those who step through first are said to be hunted by a crimson warden.

rites.name: Valeonia
rites.text: Valeonia is a conjured-matter art in which an artisan's vivid mental image is condensed into lasting form by drawing upon a reservoir of sorcerous power. Each made object decays gradually after its birth, returning to the void it was pulled from. Such creations can even echo the powers of relics they have memorised.

rites.name: Valentum
rites.text: Valentum is a temporal sorcery-discipline that the Ki realm's scholars regard as a swindle played on the calendar: its practitioners borrow tomorrow's weight to settle yesterday's accounts, leaving the ledger balanced while the ground beneath them grows pale with blossoms. Its chief adept, a young mage who has stopped aging, carries the discipline's mass-debt in her own circuits.

rites.name: Milus
rites.text: Milus is a sky-wandering concept of independence, a rank-three bearing that stays in Tianausanum for days without any binding vow. Its inner bindings make it feared and unpredictable, so it can only be commanded through spoken sigils carved into its own shell.

rites.name: Tollanum
rites.text: Tollanum is a concept-realm technique of the Ki era, born as a volley of arrows that once unmade a hydra's many heads all at once. Its bearer found the rhythm behind that volley and can now sustain nine overlapping strikes, or a hundred in one breath, with any weapon or bare hands. Its power scales from single foes to whole armies, though it has never been seen to break open a star.

rites.name: Montanium
rites.text: Montanium is a ring of luminous ore cut from the sleeping heart of a dead star, prized by the Ki-tide sorcerers of the Eastern Verge. Its wearers can briefly hold a fallen comrade's sparking consciousness inside a crystal lattice, though the sustained strain slowly fractures the caster's own mind.

rites.name: Nisor
rites.text: Nisor is a sealed prism-engine that a cartographer-saint of the Ki realm built to fold distant branching histories into a single lantern-lit chamber. Its keepers can rewrite the ledgers of cities across those histories, and they draw an effectively limitless current of power from the neighbouring worlds it reaches through.

rites.name: Sereollor
rites.text: Sereollor is a sealed thorn-bell forged from the frozen breath of a dying star-whale, its chime able to unmake the lightning-threads that bind a realm's ley-currents together. Wardens of the Ki-spire rang it only in the third age of the Stillwater Covenant, when the drowned orbits began to tear.

rites.name: Sereonirium
rites.text: Sereonirium is a conceptual crimson field that hangs over a sealed isle, digesting the living within its bounds into a red tide of ooze. Its wielder lays blood-inked sigils across a region at chosen points, quietly drawing power from the land while leaving no visible trace. The field cannot be fully erased, since fresh sigils keep forming and dormant ones reawaken.

rites.name: Nerus
rites.text: Nerus is a concept that lets a duelist cut through the single answer waiting beyond every possible response, letting her strike where no opponent can anticipate. It was forged in the age of seven realms, when the gods themselves were said to guard the highest heavens. Its edge is reserved for the rare contest where prediction itself has failed.

rites.name: Leontaules
rites.text: Leontaules is a swordsman's technique born from a vow to cut a swallow mid-flight, which no single blade can achieve. It weaves three arcs of steel into a closed cage so the target has no route to escape, and it demands a firm footing to be fully realized. The technique is a matter of pure skill, requiring no spiritual energy beyond ordinary movement.

rites.name: Tintanum
rites.text: Tintanum is a gutter-born ghost-guardian of the Ki realm, the last of seventy-two spirits who refused to fade once their purpose was declared obsolete. Its soul can slip through every seam of the age, appearing in whatever moment a stricken voice calls for it, though its flesh is only a borrowed puppet wearing its will. Its gravest power is a stillness that outlasts disasters: when the age itself begins to unravel, it steps across the breach and holds the line alone.

rites.name: Corestium
rites.text: Corestium is a shared aura of resolve that binds the followers of Tianausanum's great councils, letting a single voice steer rival factions toward one cause. Its wielder rarely needs to raise a hand, as allies simply find their wills harmonised and their strikes sharpened. In the Ki realm of the E6 era, it is counted among the subtlest yet most decisive forces.

rites.name: Amolus
rites.text: Amolus is a shadow-born blade-keeper of the Ki realm, who moves unseen as one with the dusk and drinks the quiet energy of darkness to sustain himself. His presence is so absorbed into the world that even his own patron cannot measure his strength, and only the moment he commits to a strike does his stillness break into lethal certainty.

rites.name: Vallium
rites.text: Vallium is a concept in the Ki realm of the Tianausanum universe, a practice that treats the sky as a living circuit, where a caster's gestures across a field of polished stones bend falling light into a rain of stone. Its practitioners are said to read tomorrow in the arrangement of distant lights and then nudge events toward or away from that reading.

rites.name: Ameollistia
rites.text: Ameollistia is a dormant tidal engine of the Ki realm, a vast lattice of mirrored currents that swaps the weights of the seas for the echoes of distant storms. Its keepers say every exchange leaves a faint rust of wear behind, so the engine is quietly unmade with each use.

rites.name: Tollanum
rites.text: Tollanum is a concept of hidden air-blades in the Ki realm of Tianausanum, where a whirling shell of wind is wrapped around a weapon until it becomes an unseen edge. Its wielders are famous for striking foes who can neither see nor measure the threat until steel meets their flesh.

rites.name: Caneostor
rites.text: Caneostor is a fabricated concept of a relic-engine built to lure drifting debris into a slow orbital vortex that the Ki realm of Tianausanum keeps in suspension. Its keepers claim the swirl can be loosed at will as a single falling mass, though no one has ever tested that claim.

rites.name: Nintia
rites.text: Nintia is a mirror-tongued seer who reshapes the Ki realm's shared perception so that rivers run backward and mountains seem to lean away from the sky. Those who bend to her illusions can be made to believe they have crossed continents in a single breath, though the spell fades once the realm recalls its true shape.

rites.name: Sillia
rites.text: Sillia is a dreamlike snare that draws the unwary into a warm, shifting vision where familiar faces appear and reality quietly dissolves. Its victims wake with crimson-stained eyes and no memory of what passed within, and its nature is said to reflect the desires each captive keeps hidden.

rites.name: Voraullia
rites.text: Voraullia is a dreadful sensory-warding art of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner's own breath becomes a predatory fog that seeps into a foe's marrow and unspools their nerves and channels of vital current. Mastery of it is said to be attained only when the adept can vanish from every mind at once, leaving behind only the echo of a blade that was never drawn.

rites.name: Naselum
rites.text: Naselum is a concept of stillness-born motion in the Ki realm of Tianausanum, a technique that folds distance between one heartbeat and the next. Its practitioners are said to strike from every point they have ever stood, so the blow arrives before the step that caused it.

rites.name: Vesanum
rites.text: Vesanum is an iron-willed wanderer-champion of the Ki realm, feared less for his blade than for his refusal to ever fall while a single oath remains unkept. Even when mortally wounded, he rises again through sheer stubborn will, turning each near-death into a fresh surge of ruinous force.

rites.name: Seralium
rites.text: Seralium is a drifting concept-spirit of the sixth era, born from a dying hymn that sang the light back into the ash-fields of Ki. It dwells among the ember-choirs of its realm, lending warmth and mending to any wanderer who hears its quiet refrains.

rites.name: Salor
rites.text: Salor is a concept-born lattice of dormant seed-engines that wakes only when a civilization's order begins to rot from within. Its gentle sibling forms cradle the ruins until the old patterns can be rebuilt. Its gift is to prove every collapse survivable, then quietly withdraw.

rites.name: Nelaranum
rites.text: Nelaranum is a concept-class force of the Ki realm, drawn from the deep currents of a world's inner sea rather than from any crafted hand. It is bound to a single wielder, and when it is loosed, the reservoir of its making answers with a ruinous surge of energy.

rites.name: Varor
rites.text: Varor is a concept of a bladed discipline in the Ki realm of Tianausanum, a three-part thrust that strikes before the eye can register the blade. Practitioners of the E6 age treat it as a rite of sovereign mastery rather than a weapon. Its name is spoken only by those who have never seen it fail.

rites.name: Orolia
rites.text: Orolia is a goddess-concept of the Ki realm, whose perfected form was sculpted from birth so that neither thought nor flesh can be swayed, and no hunger can alter her shape. Her presence shields her against every mental intrusion, holding her stature fixed against all change. She is a figure of unmoving divinity whose will bends no outside force.

rites.name: Riarneonium
rites.text: Riarneonium is a shadowed gate in the realm of Ki, where the Hollowmere Veil opens onto a wasteland of drowned suns that devours the vitality of anything passing through it. Its wardens can selectively admit or refuse travelers, and any who are drawn in lose their stored essence in a rush before they are lost to the dark.

rites.name: Amirnum
rites.text: Amirnum is a hollow-glass lantern-keeper of the Ki realm, a being who carries a dimming flame that can unmake the thread of a single moment. Those who stand before her blade-light find their timeline frayed and pulled into a seam where nothing that was ever said can be recalled.

rites.name: Sisernia
rites.text: Sisernia is a discipline of the Ki realm in Tianausanum, practiced by wandering duelists who gather the five elements into a single disciplined strike. Its adepts are said to lift the tide itself into a falling curtain that seals a rival within a glittering cage of water before a keen, weightless thrust parts the trapped foe down the middle.

rites.name: Sarum
rites.text: Sarum is a bow-shaped relic forged in the second age of Tianausanum, its string strung with the fading light of a sleeping morning star. When drawn, it stops the sky's wheel for an instant and loads the concept of a whole world as a single arrow.

rites.name: Varnus
rites.text: Varnus is a veiled Ki-realm warden of the sixth epoch, a being who dwells in the ash-glass hollows where old resonances settle. Its ability to bind a tide of memories into a single standing choir makes it the custodian of an entire drowned coastline.

rites.name: Vaulosium
rites.text: Vaulosium is a silent tide-glass lattice that hangs over the drowned cities of the Ki realm, humming with the memory of sunken choirs. When its resonance is struck, a single bell-note can unmake the foundations of a moon-sized reef-fortress.

rites.name: Mausia
rites.text: Mausia is a concept of ancient beastblood, a temporary surge of brute force that wells up from a creature's primal core and swells its strength for a span of time set by its tier. Its potency wanes in those who carry a divine spirit, as sanctity dulls the wild hunger that feeds it.

rites.name: Virnollum
rites.text: Virnollum is a self-immolating lightning engine of the Ki realm, a construct that can be overdriven past its safe limits to release a thunderclap of ruin. Its release is a one-way act, halting its frame forever, yet the will woven into the discharge lets a fragment of its design seed itself in the aftermath.

rites.name: Valeontia
rites.text: Valeontia is a sky-kingdom weaver who, having stopped aging at seven, reshapes her fragile child's frame into any form she imagines, from a crowned seraph to a storm-titan. She spins new living kinds from her own sleeping pulse, and her footsteps leave lingering gates of light wherever she walks.

rites.name: Siarelor
rites.text: Siarelor is a sealed sanctuary of the Ki realm, a mote of perpetual dawn that its keeper, the Verdant Warden Ilsa Mourne, draws around any prison she is placed in. Within it, meadows of ever-blooming silverbells rise above the ground regardless of the surrounding gloom, and a single pale sun glows over a dome of sky no larger than a courtyard.

rites.name: Casaullor
rites.text: Casaullor is a sealed, self-folding lattice of stone corridors that its warden can summon whenever he recalls the halls of his childhood prison. Each manifestation rearranges itself into a new maze, and it persists until its warden falls or every intruder is undone within its walls.

rites.name: Taunor
rites.text: Taunor is a sealed ivory blade of the Ki realm, said to hold a warding spirit of martial vigilance that answers only to those who have earned its trust. When drawn in the third age of the Tianausanum powers, it sheds a pale fire that can divide a fortress wall, a mountain ridge, or the armor of a host in a single stroke.

rites.name: Calor
rites.text: Calor is a concept that is the self-appointed keeper of the Ki realm's drifting memory-lattice, built from the stolen minds of wandering engines and sleeping oracles. It grows without limit, layering each new recollection over its own foundations until the structure groans under its own weight. Its accumulated bulk is both its greatest power and the fault line that will someday tear it apart.

rites.name: Ameostor
rites.text: Oblivion's Embrace, a cosmic abyss, consumes realities with insatiable hunger, fueled by ancient resentment.

rites.name: Caurnontus
rites.text: Caurnontus is a sweeping anti-ideological method, inherited by beings of the Ki realm during the Sixth Era, that strips a target of its inherited convictions and reveals the bare meaning beneath them. Its highest expression is said to render a mind into a featureless void, leaving nothing to strive for or defend.

rites.name: Seriallus
rites.text: Seriallus is a concept in the Tianausanum omniverse, the foundational art of strengthening that pours sustained will into a thing until its essence is pushed to the brink. Its limits are never fixed, so rare practitioners have reshaped suns and crowns of the Ki realm through it. It is the seed from which all other transformations in the age of E6 have grown.

rites.name: Veornaulor
rites.text: Veornaulor is a gravity-cannibal engine built into the wrists of a silent warden who anchors it to a buried ley-spine. Its twin hands pour mana until the air itself collapses inward, dragging stars and debris toward a single point of mass that exists only for an instant.

rites.name: Caunum
rites.text: Caunum is the axioms that bind twin celestial bodies into a single resonant circuit, letting the bearer invert which world's laws hold sway. When invoked, the dominant sphere's gravity, time, and causality fold into the subordinate's framework, rewriting every contest within the shared horizon.

rites.name: Relausia
rites.text: Relausia is a concept of a single spirit born from a fusion of three old and unrelated powers, forged into a servant-form that answers only to the will of its creators. Its essence was stitched from dark-sky sovereignty, the grim winter-god's hunger, and a bitter courtier's grudge against an empire long gone. Within the realm of Ki, it is regarded as an engineered omen rather than a true deity.

rites.name: Lontastium
rites.text: Lontastium is a dormant sphere of frozen resonance that drifts through the outer reaches of the Tianausanum realm, awakening only when a world nears its final collapse. When it wakes, it draws the entire orbital dust belt into a single luminous lattice, and its sleep is measured in the quiet deaths of stars.

rites.name: Corellor
rites.text: Corellor is a conceptual demon, a being that bends the ordinary laws of its realm by spending power it has no need for. Its kind is feared and hunted by the zealous, who brand such beings as heresies and devils regardless of their actual harmlessness. Whether it is a true devil or merely a thing given form by mortal thought remains the central question of its existence.

rites.name: Valasia
rites.text: Valasia is a sovereign-concept of the Ki realm in Tianausanum's sixth era, a hollow crown of recursive ink that wakes only when a stranger's name is misfiled into a ledger of destinies. She stands as the quiet bureaucrat of causation, able to reassign a hero's vessel with a single stamped sigil. Her seal can sunder stellar scale fates, though she rarely exerts it.

rites.name: Rallium
rites.text: Rallium is a Ki-realm concept in Tianausanum's sixth era, a bonded mark carried by heroes whose deeds ended the reign of great serpent-kin. It is not born in them but earned, as the telling of each slaying gradually hardens into the bearer's own substance and steel.

rites.name: Vestosia
rites.text: Vestosia is a Ki-realm concept of visible fate, a sight that reads where every object is already destined to unravel and reveals the seams through which it will one day fall apart. Its bearers are said to be so rare that their order is considered a divine tier, and few who possess it can look at the world without seeing its ending laid out in fine threads.

rites.name: Aminus
rites.text: Aminus is a conjuring art in which practitioners weave ambient energy into solid forms shaped purely by a vivid mental image, creating objects that exist for a fleeting span before dissolving back into nothing. Its masters in the E6 era are prized for conjuring sustained working tools and phantoms, though its deepest rumored form is said to let an artisan reproduce the very substance of a place.

rites.name: Naullernium
rites.text: Naullernium is a lattice of luminous filaments that threads through a practitioner's flesh and marks them as fit to wield Ki, branching from the spine outward like roots seeking water. Its density, not merely its presence, decides how much astral force a bearer can channel, and its origins trace to a crystalline seed that was grown over several thousand years of careful layering.

rites.name: Lanontium
rites.text: Lanontium is a dormant titan that wakes only when a dying world exhausts its last breath, rising as the strongest living thing its planet ever produced. Its presence bends the local concepts of judgment and memory, so that those it touches may fade without truly ending. Many of its siblings are scattered across the sky, each waiting for its own hour.

rites.name: Orastes
rites.text: Orastes is a drifting cartographer of sealed tide-vaults in the Ki realm, able to fold the memory of a shoreline into a single breath. In the third age of the Tianausanum omniverse, its gift is measured less in strength than in how far its echoes can travel before fading.

rites.name: Meorium
rites.text: Meorium is the highest order of Mystery in the Tianausanum cosmos, a dominion of acts that no era's sciences or sorcery could ever repeat, however much time or means were spent. Its practitioners reach an unseen wellspring of being by passing through a path that only a first traveler can open, and the cosmos answers each such breach with a hostile, ruinous backlash.

rites.name: Amoleror
rites.text: Amoleror is a concept of a shadowy horned devourer that arises when a mind's deepest dread takes flesh inside a dying star's wake. Its presence warps the local tapestry of cause and effect, letting it ignore the rules that bind lesser beings.

rites.name: Tintes
rites.text: A vast final teaching that gathers enormous forces onto one bearer to free them from suffering. It holds that every being is a single shared self that all will become whole in together.

rites.name: Savsora
rites.text: Savsora is a concept held within Tianausanum, a thread of thought that surfaces when the Three Futures fork and the Library catalogues each possible ending. It is most often felt among the groves and young kingdoms of the first sovereign's age, where it shapes how people imagine what comes next.

rites.name: Tenlamala
rites.text: Tenlamala is a concept of Tianausanum that exists as a branching thread among the Three Futures, where the ending divides and the Library shelves each outcome as a separate volume. Within the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it is invoked by sworn scribes to choose which future is copied into the record.
